images.title: Folding a circle in half
images.purpose: Show that folding a paper circle in half gives a semicircle of 180°, and folding again gives two equal 90° parts.
images.composition: A round paper circle on the left and a semicircle on the right, with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round paper circle with a teal #0072B2 outline, cut by one straight line into 2 equal halves. Right: one half of that circle as a semicircle with its straight edge at the bottom, and one grey #6B7280 crease from the centre straight up, splitting it into 2 equal quarter circles. Exactly 2 shapes and 1 crease.

images.description: One full circle marked 360° and one semicircle marked 180° whose single crease makes two equal parts of 90° each.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what the circle becomes after each fold and what happens to the angle.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
